confirmed.suspectedCause: Sift's load-time work on YouTube (round 12's progressive first look and sliced list drawing, plus generic helpers like findDialog, findNav and visible running on an adapter page, and font loading) competes with YouTube's own rendering on a busy main thread. YouTube's first grid or result row then paints later. Sift waits for that row, so its list is late too. The round 12 merge is the likely trigger, since round 12 base measured +132 / -180 ms.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but the gap is about half what was claimed. Severity is medium, not high. firstpaint.ts on 9461, Sift off and on in turns, medians (load average 1 to 4, other test Chromes running). Home (ytd-rich-item-renderer --sift li.item): 3 runs per side gave +56 ms, then 5 runs gave +293 and +579 ms (original 2044/2367/2473 vs Sift 2100/2660/3052). Search 'gluten free bread' (ytd-video-renderer), 5 runs per side, twice: original 2384 vs Sift 2961 (+577), and 1975 vs 2647 (+672). Search 'rick astley': 2314 vs 2845 (+531). So Sift's first list entry comes 0.3 to 0.7 s later (1.1x to 1.3x), not 0.8 to 1.9 s. In every Sift-on run, the original's first renderer appeared in the same frame as Sift's list. So YouTube's own row is delayed when Sift is on. DOMContentLoaded is also later with Sift on (search: about 1400-1730 ms on vs 970-1350 off). Sift's Loading line shows at 0.86-1.3 s, before the original's first contentful paint. V8 trace of the first 2.3 s of the search load: Sift's content.js took 127 ms with Sift on and about 3 ms with it off (loadFont 26, openAtPost 9, run 8, dialogIn 7). Over 4.5 s it took 77-191 ms on vs about 70 ms off, and those traces were noisy. Sift's JS time alone is smaller than the delay, so the exact cause is not pinned down. Regression not verified: the round 12 base numbers in STATUS.md (+132 / -180) were taken at load average 6 to 12 with wide ranges, and I did not build the base.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts boot/schedule: on a YouTube adapter page, before the adapter has its first entry, do not run the full extraction pass on every mutation batch. Skip generic helpers such as dialogIn/findDialog, watchShadows, openAtPost and fillScreen, and wait cheaply for the first ytd-rich-item-renderer / ytd-video-renderer instead. Defer loadFont (two woff2 fetches plus FontFace.load) until after the first list draw or to requestIdleCallback. Re-measure with firstpaint.ts, 5 runs, on home and search. Build the round 12 base to settle the regression question.

confirmed.title: English home: a foreign title still shows with no English line when the model answers in the title's language (F1231 remainder)
confirmed.where: https://www.youtube.com/ (English), home list one-liners; src/background/index.ts doLines (lineFits failure path)
confirmed.evidence: In each 24-entry English home load, 1 to 2 Persian entries kept only their Persian title, for example 'ازدواجی وحشتناک در گیلان 😨 که بعد از شنیدن داستانش تا چند روز خوابم نبرد'. 'بررسی آپدیت جدید سامسونگ One UI 9' had the same keep-title. Nothing is lost against the original, but these entries miss the one-line description in the page's language. The 1-day expiry means a later visit retries.

The feed is personalized, so the titles vary.
confirmed.suspectedCause: doLines: when lineFits rejects a line for its language, keepTitle(m, DAY) is saved without retrying the next model in the chain, or the same model with a firmer language instruction.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced live and by mock. This is the same defect as the F1231 remainder, so track it once. Live: the current English home feed had no Persian titles, and 2 direct requests (4 Persian titles, lang en, gpt-6-luna) all came back in English. An English YouTube search with Persian results did reproduce it: results?search_query='بررسی آپدیت سامسونگ' (page lang en). Sift showed 9 of about 22 Persian rows with only the Persian title. After deleting their keep-title entries and capturing the worker's model calls (aicap.ts), the model answered in Persian for 8 entries. Most of them had long Persian description text in their context. Examples: 'بررسی تغییرات و قابلیت‌های جدید آپدیت One UI 9 سامسونگ' and '۱۰ ویژگی سامسونگ برای استفاده از قابلیت‌های گوشی'. No other model was asked for them. Sift then showed 'بررسی آپدیت جدید سامسونگ One UI 9' and 'بررسی آپدیت One UI 9 سامسونگ؛ …' with no English line. The cache held '\0keep-title' with exp = ts + 24 h. Mock: I replaced the worker's fetch so every model call answers in Persian, then sent one lang 'en' item. Result: one model call (openai/gpt-6-luna), reply {done:true} with no line, and keep-title cached for 24 h. In code (src/background/index.ts emit in doLines), done.add(id) runs before lineFits. On failure, keepTitle(m, DAY) runs, so the entry is never in r.left and never retried. Nothing is lost against the original, so medium at the low end. Side note, not claimed: one cached line was itself Persian ('تغییرات آپدیت Samsung One UI 6.0', about half Latin letters) and was shown on the English page, so lineFits let a mixed-script wrong-language line through.
confirmed.fix: src/background/index.ts doLines/ask emit: when lineFits fails on language, do not keepTitle at once. Collect the entry and re-ask once, either with the language spelled out (langName(want), e.g. 'English', and a note to ignore the context's language) or with the next model in the chain. Call keepTitle(m, DAY) only if that retry also fails. Optionally pass the language name, not just the 'en' code, in the per-item input and LINES_SYSTEM. Also tighten lineFits/scriptFits so a line whose non-Latin letters are in the title's script does not pass for 'en'.

confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on both Guardian articles. confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on https://www.usatoday.com/. 16 Sift links end in '…', and 14 of them have the full headline in the original link's title attribute. Examples: 'Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on original Star Trek…' (title ends ', has died at 90') and 'How did high-speed passenger trains collide? Nearly 70…' (title '…Nearly 70 dead in Spain crash'). The site writes the cut-off text into the DOM, but its links keep the full title, which shows on hover. Pooled over 10 runs a side: 301 vs 578 ms, +277 ms. GitHub file ('.react-code-text', --sift pre, 5 runs, twice): 597 vs 937 ms, then 383 vs 564 ms. Pooled: 469 vs 772 ms, +303 ms. GitHub repo ('table[aria-labelledby=folders-and-files]', --sift table): 463 vs 951 ms (+488), then 827 vs 1282 ms (+455). GitHub issues list (--sift li.item): 372 vs 711 ms (+339), then 1049 vs 1782 ms (+733). Every Sift-on run was later than the Sift-off median. DOMContentLoaded moves later with Sift on: Bread 1250-2470 vs 494-931 ms. Long tasks before content: Bread 93-695 ms on vs 0-76 ms off; GitHub file 190-785 vs 0-241 ms. With Sift on, the original's own code element was often ready at 257-470 ms, while Sift's pre came at 432-1249 ms. The ratio is 1.5-2.1x, not 2.8x, but the added 0.2-0.5 s holds. Control: MDN toUpperCase 136 vs 166 ms, equal as claimed. I did not recheck OSM. A load profile with Sift on (scratchpad skn0/loadprof.ts) puts most of the time in Sift. On the GitHub blob, extract runs several times during parsing (schedule2, MutationObserver and loadedAgain), about 715 ms inclusive under the profiler. findTop takes 189 ms and leadHeadingEl 88 ms, mostly forced layout. confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts schedule()/run(): while document.readyState is 'loading' and a first view already shows the page's main block, do not re-extract on every mutation batch; wait until DOMContentLoaded. Defer openAtPost, processAi and the table fit() pass (ui) until after the first paint, using requestIdleCallback. In generic.ts, cache findTop() (line ~6862) and leadHeadingEl per run, or skip their getBoundingClientRect calls during parsing. Track this under F1300's within-100-ms target rather than as a new high finding.
